preamble: Implosivization of a voiced coronal stop: [d] becomes the implosive [ɗ]. In Sindhi, Middle Indo-Aryan initial d- and geminate -dd- became the dental implosive ɗ (Sindhi ڏ), part of the change that also gave ɓ, ʄ and ɠ (Masica 1991); Sanskrit danta 'tooth' > Sindhi ɗandu is the textbook case. Saraiki shares the change, but its coronal implosive is retroflex [ᶑ], so it is not counted here. In Vietnamese, Proto-Vietic *d also ends up as đ [ʔɗ] (đực 'male' < *dək), but only via devoicing to t and then t > ɗ (see t > ɗ), so it is not listed as a direct case.
sources: Masica, C. P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press.
Ferlus, M. (1992). Histoire abrégée de l'évolution des consonnes initiales du Vietnamien et du Sino-Vietnamien. Mon-Khmer Studies 20, 111–125. https://halshs.archives-ouvertes.fr/halshs-00923038
